The Coppa Italia brought a fascinating clash between Parma and Catania on August 14, 2026, as both sides aimed to secure their place in the next round of the tournament. The atmosphere was charged with expectation for a match that promised tactical depth and individual brilliance. Lontani's First-Half Masterclass Parma took control of the proceedings early on, utilizing high pressure to disrupt Catania 's buildup play. After initial efforts from Adrián Bernabé and El Bilal Touré , the deadlock was finally broken in the 19th minute. Following a corner delivered by Emanuele Valeri , the ball fell to Simone Lontani , who fired a precise right-footed shot into the top right corner to give the hosts the lead. Catania attempted to respond immediately and nearly equalized in the 24th minute when Simone Leonardi tested the reflexes of Edoardo Corvi with a dangerous strike. However, it was Parma who struck again during a lethal counter-attack in the 35th minute. El Bilal Touré burst forward and provided a perfect cross for Simone Lontani , who made no mistake from close range to double his tally and the lead before the break. Management and Defensive Resilience Returning from the locker rooms, Catania introduced tactical changes with the arrivals of Alessandro Raimo and Michael Liguori to try and alter the course of the match. The Sicilian side came close to reducing the deficit through an Andrea Allegretto header, but Edoardo Corvi shone again with a steady save in the bottom corner. Catania goalkeeper Filippo Rinaldi also played a key role in preventing a heavier scoreline, stopping dangerous attempts from Enrico Delprato and Sascha Britschgi . In the final stages, the tempo slowed as both managers turned to their benches, including the introductions of Mandela Keita and Franco Carboni for Parma . Despite Catania 's late efforts, the home defense remained solid, securing a professional victory and progression to the next stage.

The Coppa Italia campaign kicked off with a high-stakes encounter on August 14, 2026 , as Cagliari played host to a resilient Arezzo side. With both teams desperate to advance in the prestigious knockout competition, the atmosphere was electric from the opening whistle. Deiola Breaks the Deadlock Cagliari signaled their intent early on, coming agonizingly close to an opener in the 15th minute when both Alessandro Deiola and Paul Mendy struck the post in quick succession. The pressure eventually told in the 18th minute when Deiola was fouled inside the box by Alessandro Renzi . The captain took responsibility himself, stepping up to the spot and calmly slotting a right-footed shot into the bottom left corner to give his side the lead in the 23rd minute. Arezzo refused to be intimidated and grew into the game as the first half drew to a close. They nearly found an equalizer in stoppage time when Luca Chierico met a cross with a powerful header, but Cagliari goalkeeper Elia Caprile produced a stunning save in the top right corner to preserve the advantage heading into the break. Defensive Resilience and Late Scares The second half saw Arezzo throw everything forward in search of a way back. Mattia Sala tested Caprile again in the 62nd minute, while a VAR review shortly after denied the visitors a penalty, keeping the tension at a boiling point. Despite the introduction of fresh legs like Daniel Maldini and Matteo Prati , Cagliari struggled to find a second goal to kill off the tie, with Arezzo goalkeeper Alessandro Nunziante making vital saves from Mattia Felici and Gennaro Borrelli . As the clock ticked deep into ten minutes of added time, Arezzo launched one final assault. A header from Julián Illanes was bravely blocked by the Sardo defense, and Andrea Cagnano sent a late effort high and wide. After a grueling battle, Cagliari held firm to secure their place in the next round, surviving a spirited challenge from their lower-league opponents.

matches.title: Monza vs Avellino
matches.description: Watch Monza vs Avellino highlights and goals from Coppa Italia on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on August 14, 2026. The Coppa Italia returned to action on August 14, 2026, as Monza hosted Avellino in a knockout tie filled with high expectations. Both sides looked to make an early statement in the competition, setting the stage for a tactical battle under the lights. Varela’s First-Half Masterclass Monza established their dominance from the opening whistle, pinning Avellino back with relentless attacking sequences. The creative hub of Patrick Cutrone and Omari Forson was at the heart of everything, constantly probing a stretched defensive line. After several near-misses and desperate blocks from the visitors, the deadlock was finally broken in the 22nd minute. Gustavo Varela showcased his clinical instincts, finding the bottom left corner with a sharp left-footed strike from the center of the box to give the hosts a deserved lead. Avellino struggled to find an answer to Monza ’s fluid movement. Just as the first half seemed to be drawing to a close, the home side struck again to double their cushion. In the 45th minute, Patrick Cutrone turned provider, delivering a precise ball to Gustavo Varela , who calmly slotted home his second goal of the match into the bottom right corner. The brace from the young attacker sent Monza into the break with a commanding two-goal advantage and all the momentum. Forson Seals the Deal There was no let-up from the hosts as the second half commenced. Within six minutes of the restart, the match was effectively put to bed. Patrick Cutrone , continuing his exceptional display of playmaking, threaded a perfect through ball to Omari Forson . The winger made no mistake, firing a left-footed shot into the top right corner to make it 3-0. The goal allowed Monza to manage the game, leading to a flurry of substitutions including the introduction of Andrea Colpani and Andrea Petagna . Despite the deficit, Avellino showed glimpses of fight. Luca Pandolfi and Andrea Favilli both tested the Monza backline, with goalkeeper Demba Thiam called into action to preserve his clean sheet. Avellino 's frustration began to show late on, as Dimitrios Sounas received a yellow card for a heavy challenge in stoppage time. Professional Finish to the Tie In the dying moments, Andrea Colpani nearly added a fourth with a curling free-kick that whistled just over the crossbar. However, the work had already been done. The final whistle confirmed a comprehensive 3-0 victory for Monza , a result built on the predatory finishing of Gustavo Varela and the sublime vision of Patrick Cutrone , who ended the match with three assists. For Avellino , it was a difficult exit from the tournament, while Monza marches on to the next round with confidence.

Fiorentina's relentless pressure left the visitors struggling to find answers in a chaotic opening to the period. Consolation and Professional Closing Benevento did manage to find a spark of hope in the 54th minute when Davide Lamesta unleashed a powerful strike from outside the box to beat De Gea .
